scope: Proposition 9.1 (Second split) of the manuscript “Generalized Star Height at Most Three” (preprints/Generalized-Star-Height-at-Most-Three-September-25-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 134 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eeae440333d912ab), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the updates Ge on D, the languages e Px, e Qy satisfy: 1. on a word in D∗, every match of e Px e Qy from its beginning consumes exactly the first episode e and has Ge(x) = y; 2. every e ∈ D admits such a split for every input x ∈ U. Thus this split has empty skip domain.
